title: GitHub Actions workflows: default to GITHUB_TOKEN for same-repo steps; use a GitHub App token only for cross-repo access, separate credential scope, or re-triggering workflows
answers: Which token should a workflow step use to comment on an issue or PR with gh?
Why doesn't a comment or label my workflow creates start another workflow?
Can a GitHub Actions job use GITHUB_TOKEN to access a different repository?
Where are the repo rules on when to use actions/create-github-app-token?
body:
Path: GitHub Actions workflow authoring in .github/workflows/ for steps that call the gh CLI, comment on issues/PRs, push, or touch other repositories; the guidance is the "Prefer GITHUB_TOKEN When Its Scope and Trigger Behavior Are Sufficient" section of .claude/rules/github-actions.md.
Rule: Use `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` by default for operations in the current repository when the job's `permissions:` are sufficient. Reach for `actions/create-github-app-token` (consumed as `steps.<id>.outputs.token`) only when the step needs other repositories, separately scoped credentials, or must produce an event that triggers another workflow, because events created with GITHUB_TOKEN generally do not start workflow runs.
Constraints: Applies to choosing the token per step. Does not apply when the operation needs cross-repo access or step-level privilege isolation; the repo's build-docs.yml (cross-repo steps) and ui-review.yml (step-scoped token) still rely on App tokens. Check what the operation actually needs rather than defaulting to GITHUB_TOKEN; the rule's bad/good YAML pair shows a comment that needs no re-trigger.
applies: Repo-wide guidance for choosing the token in GitHub Actions workflows and workflow-authoring rules; not a rule about the runtime behavior of any single workflow file.
says: Why does an automated label or comment fail to trigger downstream workflows?
Allow automated repository tasks to trigger secondary workflow runs after posting comments.
An automated workflow task cannot access external repositories with standard repository credentials.
Choose between standard repository tokens and custom application credentials for automated tasks.
search: Workflow steps in `.github/workflows/` should default to `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` for same-repository operations when job `permissions:` suffice, as defined in `.claude/rules/github-actions.md`. Use `actions/create-github-app-token` (`steps.<id>.outputs.token`) only when a step requires cross-repository access, step-level privilege isolation, or must trigger downstream workflows that `GITHUB_TOKEN` events cannot start. Existing workflows like `build-docs.yml` (cross-repo steps) and `ui-review.yml` (step-scoped credentials) retain App tokens based on actual operational needs.
